item.title: Vortex matter as a magnetically programmable metasurface for tuning near-field radiative heat transfer
item.description: arXiv:2610.26874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) is of great interest for energy conversion and thermal management. Recent work on NFRHT has shown that metasurfaces can enhance NFRHT and reshape its spectral characteristics. Here, we show that the vortex lattice of a type-II superconductor represents a self-assembled metasurface whose lattice dimensions, in contrast to most other metasurfaces, can be tuned by magnetic fields, allowing NFRHT to be varied by orders of magnitude. Specifically, we show that for two Nb surfaces at 4.2 K and separated by a 100 nm gap, NFRHT can be magnetically tuned by a factor >200. Further, we show that the tuning range grows upon cooling, exceeding 10^5 at 2 K, which is far beyond the order-unity modulation of many proposed schemes for tuning NFRHT. Our results establish vortex matter as a magnetically programmable thermal metasurface and open new opportunities for tuning the flow of heat at the nanoscale.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Sangi, Pramod Reddy, Shanhui Fan

item.title: High-Field and Light-Dependent Magnetization Provides Evidence for Coexisting Granular Superconductivity and Superparamagnetism in Nitrogen-Doped Diamond
item.description: arXiv:2610.26880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigated the field-, temperature-, and time-dependent magnetic moment of a nitrogen-doped type Ib diamond in darkness and under monochromatic light with a low laser intensity of about 160 $\mu$W cm$^{-2}$. In darkness, below approximately 25 K, the magnetic moment exhibits unconventional hysteresis loops that can be explained by the coexistence of superparamagnetism and superconductivity in certain regions of the sample. Under illumination, this hysteresis largely disappears, leaving mainly the superparamagnetic contribution. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal an irreversibility below 25 K in darkness, which vanishes under illumination. Similarly, at 0.5 T and below 25 K, the time-dependent magnetization shows flux-creep-like behavior that disappears when the sample is illuminated. All light-induced changes are fully reversible: the magnetic properties measured in darkness are restored after the sample is heated above roughly 50 K. Removing the superparamagnetic contribution from magnetization measurements up to $\pm 14$ T reveals clear characteristics of a granular superconductor, namely, a well-defined penetration field $H_p \approx 2.6$ T and a critical field $H_{c2} \approx 10.6$ T. Based on theoretical considerations, we attribute the observed phenomena to the combined effects of internal stress and local variations in nitrogen concentration within localized regions that can be regarded as grains. This interpretation is supported by Raman and birefringence spectroscopy measurements on the same sample.
item.dc:creator: E. Osmic, J. Barzola-Quiquia, S. Winnerl, T. Herrmannsdoerfer, M. Uhlarz, J. Meijer

item.title: Rashba-controlled emergence and reversal of critical-field anisotropy in p-wave magnet--superconductor hybrids
item.description: arXiv:2610.27499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that tuning Rashba spin-orbit coupling can change the in-plane field direction along which an $s$-wave superconductor is most susceptible to Zeeman depairing. We consider a two-dimensional $s$-wave superconductor subject to an odd-parity exchange field induced by a $p$-wave magnet. Without Rashba coupling, the out-of-plane exchange field enhances the in-plane critical field but leaves its angular response exactly isotropic, despite the anisotropic magnetic spin texture. Minimizing the Bogoliubov--de Gennes grand potential over uniform singlet pairing, we find that increasing Rashba coupling first generates and then reverses the principal-axis critical-field contrast, switching the minimum-critical-field direction by $90^{\circ}$. Equal principal-axis fields at the intervening compensation point coexist with residual angular modulation. We interpret the reversal through competing momentum-dependent depairing contributions from the magnetic and Rashba spin textures, while the on-site singlet pairing channel remains unchanged. Direction-dependent discontinuous collapses of the order parameter further shape the critical-field curves. These results identify a tunable directional paramagnetic response within the uniform-pairing sector. In heterostructures with sufficient electrostatic tunability of interfacial Rashba coupling, this reversal would enable gate control of the easy-depairing axis without reorienting the magnetic texture.
item.dc:creator: Rui-Xiang Cheng, Zhao Gong, Dong-Hui Xu, Chui-Zhen Chen

item.title: Pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal
item.description: arXiv:2610.27664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a model that explains the mechanism of pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal. Four types of pair potentials are assumed for a Cooper pair consisting of two electrons on different layers. Absence of local inversion symmetry gives rise to the spin-orbit coupling which is antisymmetric in the two layers. We assume that external pressure enhances the hybridization between the two layers. The stability of the superconducting states is well explained by the frequency symmetry of the induced pairing correlations by these potentials. Pressure-induced superconductivity emerges when the following two conditions are realized. (i) The spin-orbit coupling induces the odd-frequency pairing correlations and suppresses superconductivity at ambient pressure. (ii) The interplay between the spin-orbit coupling and the hybridization induces the additional pairing correlation that belongs to an even-frequency symmetry class. We briefly discuss the relevance of our model to real materials.
item.dc:creator: Tomoya Sano, Satoshi Ikegaya, Shingo Kobayashi, Yasuhiro Asano

item.title: Andreev Scattering Driven Surface Photogalvanic Effect
item.description: arXiv:2610.27683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The surface photogalvanic effect is a powerful tool for generating macroscopic direct currents in centrosymmetric film structures via asymmetric scattering of carriers at film boundaries. Here, we uncover a fundamentally distinct regime of photoinduced transport in normal metal-superconductor heterostructures, in which the macroscopic photocurrent is governed by Andreev scattering at the interface rather than by classical scattering. We demonstrate that the interplay between asymmetric surface scattering and Andreev retroreflection yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent anomalous photocurrent. Strikingly, the electron-hole conversion at the normal-superconducting interface dictates a macroscopic sign reversal of the photogalvanic current across the superconducting transition, and induces non-analytic spectral kinks exactly at the pairing gap frequency. Our results establish the Andreev reflection-driven surface photogalvanic effect as a platform for optical control of superconducting correlations and suggest a direct, non-invasive spectroscopic probe for gap dynamics in hybrid quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: V. M. Kovalev, I. G. Savenko

item.title: Non-uniform grids to accelerate electron-phonon coupling calculations for superconductivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.27718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient and accurate evaluation of electron-phonon interactions is essential for predictive superconductivity calculations, but dense Brillouin zone sampling requirements pose a major computational bottleneck. To overcome this, we introduce an accelerated, highly scalable framework that combines a double delta truncation scheme with non-uniform Farey grids in both $\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ space. The truncation strategy significantly reduces computational cost by restricting integration to states satisfying energy constraints near the Fermi level, while the Farey grids dynamically resolve sampling errors from localized scattering and stabilize convergence. Applied to elemental aluminium and several high-pressure hydrides, this combined methodology reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude and yields electron-phonon coupling constants and superconducting critical temperatures Tc typically within about 5% of full-grid benchmarks. This approach overcomes sampling bottlenecks associated with dense uniform grids, making accurate, low-cost predictions of superconductivity in complex quantum materials feasible.
item.dc:creator: Kang Wang, Siyu Chen, Sun-Woo Kim, Kieran Bozier, Chris Pickard, Bartomeu Monserrat

item.title: Superconducting weak links at substrate steps in bilayer nickelate films
item.description: arXiv:2610.27729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ambient-pressure superconductivity above 40 K has been realized in bilayer nickelate thin films on SrLaAlO$_4$ (001), yet resistive measurements often exhibit incomplete zero-resistance states and/or two-step superconducting transitions of unresolved origin. We show that these features arise from superconducting weak links at substrate step-terrace structures. A direct correlation between the azimuthal-angle-dependent two-step transition and step-terrace orientation establishes this connection, further supported by atomic-scale visualization of structurally disrupted regions at step terraces. Modeling the films as pristine (weak-link) regions with higher (lower) transition temperature reproduces essential features of the two-step transition using both a simple model and finite-element simulations. Transport measurements further reveal a strong dependence of transition characteristics - and even the occurrence of superconductivity itself - on average terrace width. These results identify step-induced weak links as the microscopic origin of two-step transitions in bilayer nickelate films, providing a framework for understanding anisotropic and percolative transport, and a route to superconducting devices.
item.dc:creator: Yidi Liu, Yaoju Tarn, Lopa Bhatt, Puhua Zhang, Joonseo Song, Berit H. Goodge, David A. Muller, Harold Y. Hwang, Yijun Yu

item.title: Saturating $T^2$ resistivity in iron-based superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2610.28240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many correlated metals exhibit a crossover from low-temperature $\rho \propto T^{2}$ behavior to a slower increase of the resistivity at elevated temperatures. Distinguishing phonon scattering from electron--electron correlations as the origin of this crossover is experimentally challenging. We introduce a simple phenomenological framework that isolates the contribution responsible for the high-temperature saturating tendency. This approach reveals a clear contrast between systems well known for the predominance of electron--phonon scattering and several iron-based superconductors. For the latter, the conductivity can be expressed as the sum of a Fermi-liquid-like term ($\propto 1/T^{2}$) and a temperature-independent component, which together describe $\rho(T)$ up to $\sim 250$ K in LiFeAs, KFe$_2$As$_2$, and KCaFe$_4$As$_4$. In FeSe, the same approach identifies a similar regime above the nematic transition, with a pronounced change toward nearly linear-in-$T$ resistivity below it. We discuss these findings in the broader context of coherence and electronic correlations in Hund's metals.
item.dc:creator: M. Lourdes Amig\'o, Jorge I. Facio

item.title: Achieving ultrahigh-temperature superfluidity in atomic Fermi gases by suppressing pairing fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26997v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Achieving room-temperature superconductivity has been a long-sought goal of both the physics community and the industry. The superfluid transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ of a Fermi system initially increases with increasing pairing strength between fermions following the mean-field prediction of the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, and is then suppressed by pairing fluctuations as the strength increases further, which prevents $T_\mathrm{c}$ from becoming high. Here we propose a mechanism for suppressing pairing fluctuations using the synergy between population imbalance and momentum space confinement in lattice systems, enabling an ultrahigh $T_\mathrm{c}$ at moderately strong attraction. We show that in a three-dimensional optical lattice, strong Pauli exclusion between paired and excess majority fermions pushes up the pair excitation energy and suppresses finite-momentum pairing fluctuations. The mechanism is general to any lattice with a finite Brillouin zone; the optimal imbalance is modest ($p\lesssim 0.1$), keeping the Zeeman field small and avoiding orbital complications. The gapped pair dispersion at moderate imbalance exponentially suppresses thermal condensate depletion, providing a testable signature. The gapped dispersion, enhanced condensate fraction, and pseudogap reduction are all accessible in present-day experiments. This work opens new avenues toward room-temperature superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Lin Sun, Qijin Chen

item.title: Learning the Geometry of Materials Space with Trained Neural Tangent Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.27412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks trained to predict materials properties learn representations whose physical content can be difficult to extract. We use the neural tangent kernel (NTK), evaluated at trained parameters, to recover the geometry learned by a network that predicts superconducting transition temperatures from elemental composition alone. Kernel ridge regression with the trained NTK closely reproduces the network's predictive performance and substantially outperforms regression with the initial kernel. Spectral analysis and multidimensional scaling reveal a geometry dominated by a small number of directions. Clustering and local neighborhood analysis organize compounds into recognizable superconducting families and connect materials with related chemical and correlated-electron properties despite substantial differences in $T_c$. These results establish trained tangent kernels as practical probes of learned materials representations, connecting property prediction with the exploration of materials space.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Kaplan, Gabriel Kotliar, Anirvan M Sengupta

item.title: Theoretical Description of Electronic Modulation and Superconducting Coherence
item.description: arXiv:2512.03368v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An electronic modulation can retain a substantial local amplitude while its translational coherence is limited by spatial disorder. Its coupling to superconductivity therefore cannot be characterized by a single modulation intensity. We develop a phenomenological formulation of a finite-wave-vector complex electronic envelope coupled to a charged superconducting field. Translation and gauge symmetries constrain the interaction terms, while amplitude, modulation-gradient and condensate-gradient couplings act on distinct responses. The resulting variational equations give uniform coexistence conditions, local stability criteria and phase-gradient coefficients. We define the helicity modulus by a boundary twist, distinguish phase-only from amplitude-weighted correlations, and give an explicit minimal spectral Hamiltonian illustrating how the electronic texture may enter momentum-resolved measurements. The proposed tests use distinct spatial, spectral and stiffness observables; none assumes that a tunnelling gap directly measures condensate amplitude. An explicit kernel expansion yields the leading displacement of the selected wave vector, while the thermodynamic twist response determines phase rigidity independently of charge intensity. The analytical relations and selected numerical responses distinguish amplitude, spatial organization and condensate rigidity within the specified coupled-field model.
item.dc:creator: Jaehwahn Kim, Davis A. Rens, Waqas Khalid, Hyunchul Kim

item.title: Exact Single-Scale Outer Solution of the Abrikosov Vortex in the Extreme Type-II Limit
item.description: arXiv:2605.25938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the exact outer structure of the Abrikosov vortex in the extreme type-II limit, which occurs when the Ginzburg-Landau parameter $\kappa$ diverges. In this limit, Ginzburg-Landau theory simplifies, outside a shrinking core, to a closed nonlinear theory for the superfluid velocity subject to an algebraic density constraint. The resulting solution is asymptotically exact everywhere outside the vanishing vortex core, demonstrating that both magnetic field and superconducting density vary on the length scale of the London penetration depth. This establishes that the conventional two-length-scale picture of the vortex does not hold in the $\kappa\gg 1$ limit.
item.dc:creator: Eugene B. Kolomeisky

item.title: Orientation-resolved tunnel spectroscopy of a triplet superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2606.04742v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although Cooper pairs in superconductors generally condense into a spin-singlet state, spin-triplet superconductivity has attracted sustained interest since it enables dissipationless spin transport and is an important requirement for manifold topological quantum technologies. Noncentrosymmetric superconductors provide a promising route to triplet pairing because their intrinsic antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling (ASOC) can mix spin-singlet and spin-triplet states. To date, the strongest evidence for such mixed-parity superconductivity has been reported in heavy-fermion systems, where strong electronic correlations obscure the role of ASOC. Whether ASOC alone can support a substantial spin-triplet component remains unresolved. Here we show that the weakly correlated noncentrosymmetric superconductor Nb$_{18}$Re$_{82}$ (Nb-Re) hosts a mixed-parity superconducting state with a substantial spin-triplet contribution. Orientation-resolved low-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a strongly anisotropic quasiparticle density of states. A symmetry-constrained analysis shows that the spectroscopic dataset is explained by an order parameter combining a nodal spin-singlet component with a spin-triplet contribution reaching up to half of the singlet amplitude. These findings provide a momentum-resolved determination of a mixed-parity superconducting order parameter and demonstrate that ASOC alone can foster a substantial spin-triplet component. More broadly, they establish orientation-resolved tunneling spectroscopy as a route to identifying mixed-parity superconducting states and suggest that triplet superconductivity may be more widespread among noncentrosymmetric materials than previously recognized.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Strohmeier, Andriy Smolyanyuk, Karsten Held, Michael Smidman, Geetha Balakrishnan, Wolfgang Belzig, Elke Scheer, Angelo Di Bernardo

item.title: Synthesis and stability of high-$T_c$ LaH$_{10\pm\delta}$ films at high pressures
item.description: arXiv:2608.18865v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-pressure hydrides hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures across all classes of superconductors. Currently lanthanum decahydride, LaH$_{10}$, exhibits the highest critical temperature among binaries, with $T_c \approx$ 250 K at pressures between 140-180 GPa. Here, we report the synthesis of LaH$_{10\pm\delta}$ films in two DACs at pressures of 168 GPa and 176 GPa via in situ laser heating of elemental lanthanum films with ammonia borane (NH$_3$BH$_3$) as the hydrogen donor. The high-symmetry fcc lanthanum sublattice (space group $Fm\bar3m$) is resolved using synchrotron X-ray diffraction, with unit cell parameters in excellent agreement with previous studies on bulk samples. We provide confirmation of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in LaH$_{10\pm\delta}$ with highest $T_c$ of 247 K at 176 GPa evidenced in electrical measurements. The characteristic suppression of superconductivity is observed in magnetic fields. Furthermore, combined diffraction and electrical measurements reveal remarkable temporal stability of both the crystal structure and the high-$T_c$ superconductivity over the full measurement period of about 300 days post laser heating. Our work establishes film precursors using physical vapour deposition (PVD) techniques as a practical route to hydride formation, opening a pathway toward the controlled synthesis of promising ternary hydrides and the integration of micro-fabricated device geometries in diamond anvil cells.
item.dc:creator: Sam Cross, William Thomas, Lawrence Nobbs, Rebecca Nicholls, Oliver Lord, Qian Zhang, Dominique Laniel, Max Gerin, Bjorn Wehinger, Mohamed Mezouar, Xiaojiao Liu, Egor Koemets, Annette Kleppe, Sven Friedemann, Jonathan Buhot

item.title: Universal electrical resistivity in iron-based high-temperature superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2610.23865v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity $\rho(T)$ in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of $\rho(T)$, which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the $\rho(T)$ shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that $\rho_{ab}(T)$ is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Gr\"uneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature $\Theta_D$ and the hopping activation energy $E_a$. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant $\lambda_{e-ph}$in the studied IBS.
item.dc:creator: E. F. Talantsev

item.title: Topological Charge-2ne Superconductivity and Clustering Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2512.21325v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Charge-$2ne$ superconductors condense clusters of more than two electrons, extending superconductivity beyond Cooper pairing. They exhibit distinctive signatures including fractional flux quantization $h/(2ne)$ and are actively being explored in strongly correlated systems. We develop a general framework for constructing and characterizing \emph{topological} charge-$2ne$ superconductors by combining wavefunction and field theory approaches. Generalizing the Read-Green wavefunction and Higgsing Read-Rezayi-type states yield two families that can support deconfined non-Abelian anyons and non-Abelian superconducting vortices. The first family also admits a construction from doping Jain states. Through Higgs theories, we find that the first and second families realize weak and intermediate clustering regimes, respectively, distinguished by the topology of vortices carrying flux greater than $h/(2ne)$, while strong clustering yields a charge-$2ne$ superconductor without intrinsic topological order. These reveal that higher-charge superconductivity supports a richer hierarchy of topological phases beyond the Read-Green weak-strong pairing dichotomy, with distinct internal clustering structures giving rise to different topological structures at fixed condensate charge.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Qiang Gao, Yan-Qi Wang, Hui Yang, Congjun Wu

item.title: Probabilistic denoising for reliable signal extraction in spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2605.07819v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While deep learning offers powerful capabilities for scientific research, its application is often hindered by a lack of quantitative reliability. To address this, we introduce a probabilistic denoising framework that simultaneously extracts denoised signals and element-wise predictive uncertainties from noisy data. We demonstrate this approach on three-dimensional angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy data, showing that the model reliably recovers the spectral features of a cuprate superconductor from Poisson-distributed noise with an average count of only 0.02 electrons per voxel. Crucially, we show that these predicted uncertainties can be propagated into subsequent superconducting gap analyses, enabling quantitative parameter extraction with scientifically meaningful error bars. Furthermore, we validate the broad applicability of our approach by successfully extending it to two-dimensional X-ray diffraction data. Ultimately, this approach establishes uncertainty-aware deep learning not merely as a visualization tool, but as a rigorous framework for scientific data analysis.
item.dc:creator: Younsik Kim, Changyoung Kim
